items.title: Tryst with the Constitution: On the immunity of election commissioners
items.summary: The Election Commission of India has been in the news over the past few months, particularly over questions concerning the appointment of the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) and the other election commissioners (ECs), as well as their internal decision-making. Amidst these discussions, attention has also turned to the statutory immunity granted to the commissioners, particularly, its scope, legislative intent and whether such a protection is warranted in the first place. While hearing a batch of petitions concerning the ECI, Justice Joymalya Bagchi added another dimension to this discourse by remarking that even judges do not enjoy the same immunity as election commissioners. However, the legal position is more nuanced and the nature of the ECI’s functions provides good reasons for affording its commissioners comparable protection. items.title: Saurav Ganguly moves Delhi High Court against movie Doosra, claims rights over Lord's shirtless celebration
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Thursday refused to pass any order on a plea by former India cricket captain Sourav Ganguly’s plea to stay the release of the film “Doosra”. Justice Dinesh Bhatt said the case will be heard tomorrow (Thursday). The movie is scheduled to be released in theatres tomorrow. Justice Bhatt made it clear that he has not stopped the release of the film in theatres. "I have said no stay, so the film can go on," Justice Bhatt said. Ganguly and film production house Luv Films LLP have approached the Delhi High Court seeking to restrain the release of the film citing exploitation of the former's live events, particularly his captaincy in the NatWest cricket series final and his shirtless celebration at Lord's. They have alleged unauthorised commercial exploitation of Ganguly’s personality rights and infringement of the production house’s exclusive contractual rights over his proposed biopic. Ganguly and Luv Films have sought an injunction against the film’s theatrical, digital and other releases, as well as the circulation of promotional material allegedly using Ganguly’s name, image, likeness and iconic cricketing moments without authorisation. Bora has alleged that the proceedings amount to an attempt to curb peaceful dissent and violate their fundamental rights to freedom of speech, assembly and personal liberty. items.title: Police summons over Jantar Mantar trespass: CJP leaders Saurav and Ashutosh seek time
items.summary: Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were summoned for questioning by the Delhi Police Crime Branch on Thursday, October 22, in connection with two cases registered over entry into the denotified protest site at Jantar Mantar. The notices were issued a day after the two leaders were released from Tihar Jail following an order by a Special Executive Magistrate (SEM) court. However the CJP leaders have sought for more time and did not appear today. They were asked to appear at the Rajouri Garden office of the Delhi Crime Branch at noon on Thursday. Another individual, identified as Shinde, was also summoned for questioning. The cases concern allegations of trespassing at Jantar Mantar after it was denotified as a designated protest site, obstructing police personnel on duty and disobeying a government order. The Delhi Police transferred the two cases from the local police stations to the Crime Branch, citing the sensitive nature of the matter and the need for an impartial investigation. The two leaders were released after SEM Ritu Raj accepted their personal and surety bonds and recorded their written undertakings to maintain peace and abide by the law.

items.title: Nothing wrong in call for regime change: Neha Bora to Delhi High Court in SEM notice case
items.summary: All India Students Association (AISA) president Neha Bora told the Delhi High Court on Thursday that in a democracy, there is nothing wrong in making a call for a regime change. Bora was responding to the argument by Delhi Police that they (Bora has been referred to by they/ them pronouns) were part of the gathering in which a call was made for change of regime. "Joint sitting with CJP leaders and Prashant Bhushan where it was said ye regime change ki ladai hai aur ham regime change karwa ke rahenge. She was part of the same gathering," the law officer for Delhi Police contended. "There is nothing wrong with regime change in a democracy," Bora's counsel said. "Do we need to go into that?" the Court asked. "Regime change will (have to) happen by votes, not by lumpen elements congregating in New Delhi," the Delhi Police replied. The Court was hearing a plea filed by Bora challenging a notice issued to them by the Special Executive Magistrate (SEM) directing them to execute a personal bond of ₹10,000 and maintain peace.
